records.name: North Korea
records.summary: North Korea is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely: same-sex conduct is not named in the Criminal Code, but Article 193 prohibits “decadent culture,” and broad obscene-activities provisions give the authorities unlimited discretion, and reported incidents of criminalisation and even execution for homosexuality exist. Gender identity does not exist in public life, visitors travel under constant escort and surveillance in the world's most totalitarian system, and any nonconforming presentation or discovered digital material risks detention, with no recorded protection or recognition of gender identity to offset that exposure.

sources.summary: Outright International country page (updated 12 Mar 2026): DPRK Criminal Code (1950, rev. 2009) appears to contain no penalty for consensual same-sex acts, but Art. 193 bans import/keeping/distribution of 'decadent culture' incl. sexual recordings and Art. 262 bans collective 'obscene activities'; 2014 KCNA denied homosexuality's existence; an openly gay defector published an autobiography in 2017; no documented state or non-state violence against LGBTIQ people; no registration route for LGBTI orgs.

Legal Clarity overview: sex-marker change on birth certificate/citizen card technically possible under 'unavoidable circumstances' - application to People's Security Agency plus state forensic medical evaluation, in practice requiring surgical intervention; no law explicitly bans gender-affirming care but the under-resourced health system makes hormones/surgery effectively inaccessible.

BBC Korean feature (10 Oct 2024), 'Does homosexuality exist in North Korea too?': 10 years after the UN COI report, new laws (Pyongyang Cultural Protection Act etc.) tighten control; profiles Jang Young-jin, a novelist who defected in the late 1990s and was forcibly outed, as the first publicly known gay defector; documents how a collective-over-individual regime forces DPRK sexual minorities into silent self-suppression and frames LGBT life as human-rights abuse.

US State Department 2022 Human Rights Report for North Korea: official assessment - the totalitarian regime's pervasive abuses; the report notes no specific law criminalising same-sex conduct but the regime's total control leaves no space for LGBT life.

US State Department 2020 Human Rights Report for North Korea: official assessment - no reliable information on LGBT persons; the regime's repression of all civil society is the dominant human-rights reality.
CNN (Apr 2017): 'I could not even dream: Life as a gay North Korean' — a defector's account of homosexuality's place in North Korean society and its punishment.

KCNA commentary (22 Apr 2014): state news agency rejects the UN Commission of Inquiry's DPRK human rights report as a political fabrication and personally attacks commissioner Michael Kirby as 'a disgusting old lecher with a 40-odd-year-long career of homosexuality' to discredit it - official-record evidence of the regime's hostility toward homosexuality even while denying its existence.

records.name: Palestinian Territories
records.summary:
Trans visitors face grave danger here, with a hard internal split: in the West Bank, same-sex conduct is not criminalised (Jordan's 1951 revision dropped consensual-private-sex offences, carried into the 1960 penal code applied there), but there are no protections, family/clan hostility is severe, and the Palestinian Authority has not legislated or signed key treaties. In the other part, Gaza, a 1936 British Mandate code technically allows up to 10 years for consensual same-sex acts, Hamas has executed people for alleged homosexuality, and the area is in a catastrophic war.

Trans identities are nowhere explicitly criminalised, but public-morality provisions can catch trans people, gender-affirming healthcare is essentially destroyed or unavailable, police action against a queer organisation drew rights-group condemnation, and periodic transphobic threats and attacks are reported.

sources.summary: CAIRO 51 Palestine page: Gaza (British Mandate Criminal Code Ordinance No. 74 of 1936 still in force, silent on trans identities but trans people potentially caught by public-morality provisions) vs West Bank have different penal codes; pinkwashing critique - occupation marginalises queer/trans Palestinians alongside everyone else; documented de facto oppression.

Legal Clarity: West Bank criminal law derives from the Jordanian Penal Code No. 16 of 1960 - Jordan's 1951 revision dropped consensual-private-sex offences and the 1960 code carried that forward; practical reality harsher than formal law via social/family persecution. Formal-decognition map for West Bank.

Wikipedia LGBT rights in Palestine: patchwork decriminalisation (British Mandate code in Jordan until 1951; Jordanian Penal Code no prohibition of same-sex acts applied to the West Bank; Israel stopped using the code in 1977); PA has not legislated; no explicit prohibition on trans identity; periodic transphobic threats/attacks; PA a non-signatory to key treaties.

HRW 'Audacity of Adversity' (16 Apr 2018): LGBT people across MENA finding ways to speak out - stories, cross-border alliances, national/regional movements combating homophobia and transphobia; accompanies AFE video series of activist messages of support. Regional movement context for Palestinian LGBT life.

Times of Israel: rights groups slammed Palestinian police for banning LGBTQ activity - after the police action against al-Qaws, the foundation received a wave of hate messages which activists said 'pose a serious threat' to the gay community.

HRW (11 Jun 2018), Women's Centre for Legal Aid: interviewed 12 Palestinian women identifying as lesbian/bisexual/queer - widespread discrimination and abuse in public and family settings; Gaza's 1936 Criminal Code s.152(2) punishes consensual same-sex 'carnal knowledge' by up to 10 years (vague 'unnatural offences' concepts violate privacy/non-discrimination per HRW); 1960 West Bank code analysed similarly.

Times of Israel: Israel to allow LGBT Palestinians granted temporary asylum to work - some 90 LGBT Palestinians have received temporary permits to seek refuge in Israel after fleeing violence in the territories.
